title: INDEX MATCH: look left of the key

screens.prompt: In B7, return the product name in A2:A5 for the SKU in B6 with INDEX and MATCH.

hints.syntax: MATCH finds the second price, INDEX reads the second name: =INDEX(A2:A5,MATCH(B6,B2:B5,0)).
hints.func-index: INDEX needs A2:A5 and a row number. The row number is the only thing standing between B6 and the product name.
hints.func-match: MATCH searches the prices in B2:B5 for the value in B6 and reports 2, which is where Junction box sits in A2:A5.
hints.match-exact: The price column is unsorted, so 0 is required. Without it MATCH assumes an order the column does not have.
hints.require-ref: Take the price from B6. Typing 3.25 into the formula means a corrected price never reaches the answer.
hints.value: 3.25 is the second price down in B2:B5, so the answer is the second product name, Junction box.
hints.error: A price that is not in B2:B5 leaves MATCH with #N/A, and INDEX has no row to read.

reject.why: the outer bracket is never closed, so nothing computes
answers 2, the row number, instead of the product on that row
correct product, but the row number is hardcoded instead of found
approximate match on an unsorted price column
reads the price column back, so the answer is the price again
the price typed into the formula, so a corrected price never reaches the answer
the row number was divided by zero, so INDEX never receives a row

docs.explain:
Here the answer sits to the left of the value being searched. B6 holds the price 3.25, which is the second entry in B2:B5, so MATCH returns 2. INDEX then reads the second cell of A2:A5, and B7 shows Junction box.

VLOOKUP cannot make that move. Its column count starts at the key and runs forward, so no argument reaches a column sitting before the key. Choosing the two ranges separately is what lets the lookup run left.

The zero matters even more on this sheet. The price column runs 8.5, 3.25, 2.75, 5.4, which is not sorted in either direction. Approximate search stops somewhere in that order and can read a neighbouring row. With 0, a price that is not in the list gives #N/A.

errors.text: MATCH found no exact 3.25 in B2:B5, so INDEX was handed a position that does not exist.
INDEX was pointed at a range shorter than the position MATCH returned, so the row number runs past A5.
The zero was left off, so MATCH accepted a price it never found and INDEX read a neighbouring product.

docs.atWork: A price list where you know what something cost and need the part name, which sits to the left of the price.
docs.outcome: Return a value from the left of the key with INDEX and MATCH.

seo.title: INDEX MATCH: look left of the key
seo.description: MATCH finds the row by its price, INDEX reads the name from that row, and a lookup goes left. VLOOKUP cannot do this, because it only counts forward.
